description: Pinned bytes for every file compute_conditioning_digest() hashes, and a URL a fresh box can get each one from. See terrain_service/conditioning_artifacts.py for why each field exists.

artifacts.name: etopo_10m.tif
artifacts.note: MEASURED 2026-08-02: these bytes were NOT produced by tools/fetch_etopo.py and cannot be. The file is uncompressed (Compression=NONE; 2160x1080 float32 = 9,331,200 B + 13,775 B of tags = exactly its length) and it carries ETOPO's OWN georeferencing -- GeoAsciiParams 'WGS 84 + EGM2008 height', GDAL_NODATA '-99999', ModelPixelScale z=1.0 -- whereas fetch_etopo.py writes profile=ref.profile.copy() from wc2.1_10m_bio_1.tif, which would stamp 'WGS 84|', nodata -3.4e+38, z=0.0, and compress=deflate. Its mtime (2026-06-28) also predates fetch_etopo.py's first commit (66aecae, 2026-07-22) by 24 days. It is a gdal_translate/gdalwarp downsample of the ETOPO 2022 60s _bed product made by hand. Pixel content is _bed, confirmed: Greenland centre -151 m and West Antarctica -1360 m (the _surface product reads about +3000 m and +1800 m there). Because it has no builder and no upstream publisher, the release asset above is its ONLY representation.
artifacts.provenance: Derived from NOAA NCEI ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second _bed (doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74), a U.S. Government work in the public domain.

artifacts.name: synthetic_map_stats.json
artifacts.note: Derived from etopo_10m.tif plus the four WorldClim rasters, so it inherits etopo's drift and adds its own. Rebuilt from the real WorldClim rasters on 2026-08-01 17:45 (the previous 13,058 B copies still on the 2026-08-02 box hash a1d3a1abd05030bf and were built from FAKE climate). It holds quantile tables only -- no WorldClim pixels -- so it is redistributable where the rasters it was computed from are not.
artifacts.provenance: 64-knot quantile tables computed from etopo_10m.tif and the four WorldClim rasters.

artifacts.name: wc2.1_10m_bio_1.tif
artifacts.note: WorldClim 2.1 10m, published 2019-02-28 and byte-identical on every box measured. Upstream ships all 19 bio variables as one 49,869,449 B zip, so the source is the zip URL with a '#member' fragment; fetch_conditioning.py downloads it once per run and extracts only the four members it needs, hashing each BEFORE installing it. NOT MIRRORED on the conditioning-v1 release on purpose: worldclim.org/about.html says 'Redistribution or commercial use is not allowed without prior permission.' The pin is the check on what upstream served, not a substitute for upstream.
artifacts.provenance: WorldClim 2.1 (Fick & Hijmans 2017). Free for academic and other non-commercial use; redistribution not permitted without prior permission, hence no mirror.

artifacts.provenance: WorldClim 2.1 (Fick & Hijmans 2017). Redistribution not permitted without prior permission.

hosting.choice: GitHub release assets on this repo, under the dedicated tag 'conditioning-v1', for the two BUILT artifacts. The four WorldClim rasters keep upstream's own zip URL.
hosting.rationale: Release assets are reachable by anything that can clone this repo -- no new credential and no new bill -- and they do not enter every clone the way a committed blob or a git-lfs pointer does. The tag is dedicated and never advanced, so it carries no source meaning and nothing about a code release can move it. GitHub tags are mutable in principle; the sha256 pins make that irrelevant, because fetch_conditioning.py hashes what arrived before installing it and refuses anything else.
hosting.why_worldclim_is_not_mirrored: worldclim.org/about.html: 'The data are freely available for academic use and other non-commercial use. Redistribution or commercial use is not allowed without prior permission.' Uploading the four rasters to a public release would be redistribution. They stay on upstream's zip URL, pinned by sha256 so a substituted or corrupted download is refused exactly as a substituted release asset would be.
hosting.runner_up: The HuggingFace checkpoint repo, which is better if pods are ever cut off from github.com but not from huggingface.co. If that day comes, add its URL as a SECOND entry in each 'sources' array rather than replacing the first: the arrays are tried in order and the sha256 pin makes a second mirror free of risk.
hosting.rejected: Committing the 9,344,975 B binary into git, or git-lfs. Both are permanent in every clone forever, and git-lfs additionally adds a quota that can silently stop serving.
